editorial:
In 1950s New York, a young department-store clerk named Therese meets Carol, an elegant older woman going through a divorce. Their connection grows from a chance meeting into a deep, risky romance that could cost them everything. The movie moves slowly and quietly, letting small glances and soft conversations carry the weight. You feel the tension of a time when being yourself was dangerous, but also the warmth of two people finding each other.

The acting is excellent, especially Cate Blanchett and Rooney Mara, who make every moment feel real. The pacing is slow, so if you want fast action this might feel long. Still, the beautiful sets, costumes, and music pull you in. It is best for viewers who enjoy emotional love stories and patient storytelling. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Carol and Therese have been apart after Carol's custody battle. Therese receives an invitation to meet Carol at a restaurant. When Therese arrives, Carol is waiting. Their eyes meet across the room, and after a long pause, Therese smiles. Carol smiles back, and the film ends on that hopeful note, suggesting they are ready to try again together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow-burn romance and period dramas.
